section_guardCheck.question: Confirm the pin is a real 40-char SHA and that a malformed value would be caught. Check whether anything guards _LDT_SHA's shape; if nothing does, say so rather than adding a guard unasked.
section_guardCheck.shaShapeConfirmed: 7a739849fb16be68576ba0b9f1e397818b710614 -- length 40, matches /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/ (checked programmatically, not by eye)
section_guardCheck.wouldAMalformedValueBeCaught: NO. Read the full 168-line cloudbuild.publish.yaml. Exactly one shape guard exists in the file: the deploy DIGEST regex at the gcloud-artifacts-describe step (`[[ "$$DIGEST" =~ ^${_IMAGE}@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || { echo FATAL ...; exit 1; }`). No equivalent check exists for `_LDT_SHA`. It flows straight from the substitutions block into `git fetch --depth 1 origin ${_LDT_SHA}` (line 83) with no validation in between. A malformed value -- empty string, a branch name such as 'main' (which the dispatch explicitly says never to pin to), a truncated hash -- would either fail the fetch with an unguarded git error, or in the 'main' case, succeed silently against whatever main resolves to at build time, which is exactly the failure mode 'never pin to main' exists to prevent and nothing here enforces it mechanically.
section_guardCheck.actionTaken: none -- not asked for. Reported as required by the dispatch's verify-by-violating section.
